# 70-110 is the same conservative default the single-servo bench sketch uses.
# It is NOT the mechanical travel of any joint here. Exactly one provisional
# unloaded calibration row exists in this whole project.
# HOW TO FILL THIS IN - ONE JOINT AT A TIME:
#   1. Bench-test that joint on its own with
#      Software/emre_kalem_single_servo_bench_test
#      Documentation/HOW-TO-TEST-EACH-SERVO.md.
#   2. Find where it actually stops each way - the angle at which the joint
#      reaches a mechanical limit or the servo starts to buzz and strain.
#   3. Back off a few degrees from each end. That margin is the whole point.
#   4. Put those two numbers in min_deg and max_deg. Set home_deg to a safe
#      resting angle between them. Set calibrated to yes.
#   5. Write the same numbers into Calibration_Notes/calibration-log.csv.
#   6. In the arm console press LOAD LIMITS FILE and pick this file again.
# Only ever set calibrated=yes for a joint YOU measured. A row still sitting at
# 70-110 with calibrated=yes is a lie the console will believe and repeat
# the amber UNCALIBRATED badge is the only thing that would have warned you.
# Row joint_id=1 (shoulder) also needs mirror_mode before it can be enabled at
# all. See that row's notes.

#   sits away from 90.

#   some centre angle. If the two horns were fitted perfectly symmetrically that
#   centre is exactly 90 and the offset is 0. Horns fit on a splined shaft in
#   whole-tooth steps - about 18 degrees apart on an MG996R - so perfectly
#   symmetrical is the exception
